claims.text: The initial eutectic high-entropy alloy has dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries.
Lamellar-colony internal boundaries serve as microcrack-initiation sites during room-temperature tensile deformation.
A post-solidification low-temperature aging treatment can induce coherent nanoprecipitates.
The aging-induced coherent nanoprecipitates will form preferentially along lamellar interfaces.
Beneficial aging requires a temperature and duration sufficient for coherent precipitation but insufficient for precipitate coarsening or brittle-secondary-phase formation.
Coherent nanoprecipitates at lamellar boundaries act as effective dislocation-pinning centers.
Coherent nanoprecipitates relieve local stress concentrations at lamellar interfaces.
Dislocation pinning and local stress relief delay microcrack nucleation and propagation.
Aging-induced coherent precipitation will increase ultimate tensile strength relative to the unmodified alloy.
Aging-induced coherent precipitation will significantly improve room-temperature tensile ductility relative to the unmodified alloy.
The aged alloy will exhibit less premature microcracking than the as-cast alloy.
The as-cast baseline contains a continuous, brittle lamellar network that causes early microcrack initiation under tensile loading.
The intervention is effective only for compositions capable of forming coherent nanoprecipitates without forming coarse or brittle secondary phases.
Excessive aging temperature or duration can cause precipitate coarsening or unwanted brittle phases that negate the mechanical benefits.
The optimal aging temperature-time window for beneficial coherent precipitation in eutectic high-entropy alloys is not well defined.
The magnitudes of the predicted strength and ductility improvements remain unknown.
